rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal / predict instruction anywhere in the file; this is a pure pre-read with no live-demo beat.

All 4 content chunks (1-4) carry 3-4 bullets each with a self-contained claim; none reduces to a bare wait-state or single context-dependent fragment. Chunk 0 is a conventional title-only opener, not evaluated as an orphan.

"What would have caught this earlier?" delivers the diagnostic question. "Three failure modes you'll use to read" delivers exactly three named modes. "Why these three, every run" delivers the mechanism (statistical machine, finite window) and universality claim. "Two long ports, both surfaced all three" delivers two anchors (Ronacher, Sumner); Ronacher's bullet states all three modes showed up explicitly, and the third bullet ("Both runs held together anyway. Each had something specific in place that catches the failure modes above") extends that to Sumner's run in the plural — the header holds under the sequential read.

"Not X. Not Y. Z." sub-item HIT: chunk 1 line 5 — "Not *did the run succeed*. Not *should I have spec'd it tighter*. A diagnostic: you read the artefact, you find what went wrong, and for each thing you ask this one question." Two negated candidate framings followed by a labeled declarative is the banned triadic shape, and it is the whole slide's central move ("one tic can be the whole slide"). Other sub-items checked clean across all chunks: no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlatives, no number-plus-retraction (chunk 4's exact figures and Sumner's own "about" hedge are sourced, not a hedge-then-walk-back), no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast chunk 1 line 5 as one declarative (e.g. lead with the diagnostic and fold the two rejected framings into a single subordinate clause) instead of the two-negation build-up.
